intro: The long-horizon picture is unchanged and strengthening: the AI capex supercycle has now been validated by NVIDIA's $25B bond sale ($85B orders), SK Hynix's new ATH on a locked multi-year supply contract, and SpaceX's record IPO. Today's FOMC creates near-term noise — a hawkish dot compresses multiples temporarily — but the structural theses here are multi-quarter to multi-year and do not turn on a single dot plot. The discipline at this horizon is to use FOMC-driven dislocations as entry opportunities, not as signals to abandon. HBM supply tightness through 2028, Starlink subscriber compounding, and hyperscaler AI capex running through 2028+ are the durable drivers.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: Own the toll road on AI compute — the $25B bond sale ($85B orders) is management's public long-term conviction statement.
ideas.why: NVIDIA's first debt offering since 2021 attracted 3.4x oversubscription with $85B in institutional demand. Management funded the AI buildout with debt at this valuation — that is not a hedge, it is a declaration. The CUDA software moat, Blackwell/Rubin roadmap, SK Hynix locked as the primary memory supplier through 2030, and Apple/Google Private Cloud Compute (Siri via Blackwell B200) provide the structural demand visibility that underwrites the $299 consensus PT. At this horizon, the only question is price paid — use every FOMC-driven dip to accumulate.
ideas.driver: Hyperscaler + sovereign AI capex compounding through 2028+; inference demand following training; HBM supply locked via multi-year partnership.
ideas.risk: Custom ASICs (hyperscaler in-house chips) eroding share faster than expected; or an AI-capex digestion cycle compressing both growth and the multiple simultaneously.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: The memory leg of the AI trade — new ATH today confirms the market is pricing a multi-year supply constraint.
ideas.why: SK Hynix broke to a new ATH of ₩2,425,000 this morning, driven by the HBM shortage expected through 2028 (TradingKey) and the NVIDIA multi-year supply partnership locked through 2030. The memory industry has consolidated to three players with unprecedented pricing discipline; SK Hynix holds ~70% of NVIDIA's HBM orders; and Q1 2026 operating margin was 72% — surpassing even NVIDIA's 65%. The structural compounding story is intact: rising HBM content per GPU, ~20% secured 2026 price hikes, and a potential shareholder value enhancement program as a new catalyst.
ideas.driver: HBM4 transition and rising HBM content per next-gen GPU; disciplined three-player oligopoly; NVIDIA supply partnership through 2030.
ideas.risk: Memory is cyclical — a demand air-pocket or a Samsung capacity race would hit pricing fast despite the current oligopoly discipline.

ideas.name: Microsoft
ideas.idea: The lowest-drama way to own enterprise AI monetization — SPCX briefly overtaking its market cap is noise, not signal.
ideas.why: Microsoft monetizes AI through Azure, Copilot, and the enterprise software stack it already owns — recurring revenue from an installed base of hundreds of millions of enterprise seats. The SPCX narrative of 'SpaceX overtook MSFT intraday' is a thin-float squeeze artifact, not a fundamental displacement. Azure AI workloads are inflecting; Copilot attach rates are growing; the balance sheet is fortress-class. At $385–$395, the stock offers the most durable AI-cycle exposure per dollar of risk in the megacap cohort.
ideas.driver: Azure AI workloads + Copilot attach across the installed enterprise base; OpenAI investment appreciation.
ideas.risk: AI capex outrunning monetization for longer than expected; SPCX-driven narrative competition for 'AI infrastructure' capital allocation.

ideas.name: Alphabet
ideas.idea: Owns the full AI stack at the cohort's cheapest multiple — the re-rating thesis if search cannibalization proves manageable.
ideas.why: Alphabet has its own frontier models (Gemini), custom TPUs, a cloud business inflecting, and search cash flows funding all of it. It trades at the cheapest forward multiple in the megacap cohort because the market fears AI disrupting search. At $363–$370, the price embeds a significant probability of secular search decline that is not yet appearing in the revenue data. If Google's AI Overviews prove to be a moat-extender rather than a moat-destroyer, the re-rating is a multi-year opportunity.
ideas.driver: TPU-driven cost advantage in inference + Gemini integration across a billion-user surface; Google Cloud inflecting.
ideas.risk: Genuine query erosion to AI assistants at scale; antitrust remedies that fracture the search + advertising bundle.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: A generational franchise — post-IPO float squeeze creates the first real entry opportunity in 6–12 months.
ideas.why: SpaceX owns the only proven reusable orbital launch system at scale, a 5M+ subscriber Starlink business growing ~40%, Starshield national-security contracts, and now a nascent AI pivot via Cursor. The MSCI passive bid creates a 2–4 week float-squeeze window where price is disconnected from fundamentals. The structural move is to identify when the passive bid exhausts (monitor daily volume deceleration) and build a position as the lock-up supply doesn't arrive until December. At the right entry ($185–$200 with options hedge), this is a 3–5 year hold.
ideas.driver: Starlink subscriber and ARPU compounding toward a recurring-revenue connectivity utility; Starship driving cost-to-orbit toward near-zero.
ideas.risk: IPO-cycle overvaluation locks in a poor entry if you pay $200+ without a hedge; key-person concentration; capital intensity if Starship timelines slip.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: A sized store-of-value position — today's FOMC repricing is the kind of dip the long-term thesis is built to absorb.
ideas.why: At a multi-year horizon, Bitcoin's thesis is adoption as fixed-supply store of value, now with ETF access (IBIT, BITA), corporate treasury ownership (Strategy, MicroStrategy), and sovereign reserve conversation ongoing. The June 2026 FOMC repricing (rate hike odds 50–68%) creates a near-term headwind but does not change the four-year supply halving dynamic, the institutional access ramp, or the DXY structural weakness that is the primary macro tailwind. If today's FOMC is hawkish and BTC tests $62K–$63K, that is the structural add point, not a thesis-ender.
ideas.driver: Fixed supply meeting widening institutional access (ETFs, treasuries, corporate balance sheets) across halving cycles; Hormuz/oil disinflation → dollar lower long-term.
ideas.risk: A hawkish 2026 Fed cycle — if hike dots materialize and rates actually rise, the dollar strengthens structurally and BTC's discount rate thesis breaks down for an extended period.

ideas.name: Amazon
ideas.idea: AWS AI is the cloud-infra winner that market caps of SPCX and NVDA have temporarily obscured.
ideas.why: Amazon runs the world's largest commercial cloud (AWS), is ramping custom silicon (Trainium, Inferentia) to reduce AI inference costs for its own and third-party workloads, and has a logistics network that scales into robotic AI. SPCX briefly overtook Amazon by market cap on June 16 — a thin-float IPO artifact, not a fundamental displacement. AWS AI attach rates and Prime economics are compounding quietly while the market chases the IPO narrative. At $185–$195, AMZN is the most underappreciated AI-cycle compounder in the cohort.
ideas.driver: AWS AI workloads + Trainium/Inferentia cost advantage in inference; Prime and logistics flywheel compounding.
ideas.risk: Cloud spending deceleration if enterprise IT budgets tighten; custom silicon ramp takes longer than expected; competitive pressure from Azure and Google Cloud.
